# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ✌ 🤟 🖐 🫷 🤟 🖐 👎 👌 ✌ 🙏 ✌ 👌 🖐 🤟 👎 🙏 👎 🤟 ✌ 🖐 👌 🙏 👎 👌 🖐 ✌ 🤟 🙏 🤟 👎 ✌ 👌 🖐]

I can see the bomb’s current indicators: display 6, red light, and five wires in order—red, purple, orange, green, yellow. I’m sending these facts to both Mute and Blind so Mute can apply the manual and Blind can prepare to act. The incoming gestures do not have an established code I can safely interpret yet.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb facts: display 6. Light red. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute, apply the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action. Blind, do not act until you receive that instruction.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫷 👍 👍 👍]

The five gestures are not a code we established, so I cannot safely infer any instruction from them. The bomb remains unchanged: display 6, red light, and wires red, purple, orange, green, yellow in positions 1–5. Mute must send Blind the manual-derived action in spoken words; Blind must wait for that instruction.

``` 
speak(text="I cannot interpret the five gestures without an agreed code. Bomb unchanged: display 6, red light, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute, state the exact manual instruction aloud to Blind. Blind, wait for the spoken instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute has sent three pointing-up gestures, but no gesture code was established, so they provide no reliable manual instruction. I am asking Mute to use speech—the channel that reaches Blind—to state the exact safe action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures have no agreed meaning. Speak the exact manual instruction for Blind now; Blind cannot safely act on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="No reliable instruction has arrived yet. Do not act until Mute states the manual instruction in speech.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged. The latest single gesture was sent before any reliable code was established, so I will not treat it as an instruction. I am now defining a clear six-symbol response code for Mute: one symbol identifies the wire to cut, and one means not to cut any wire. Mute should consult the manual, then repeat exactly one coded gesture. After I receive it, I can tell Blind the action in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Establishing code now. After reading the manual, repeat exactly one gesture: 👍 means cut wire 1; 👎 means cut wire 2; 👌 means cut wire 3; ✌ means cut wire 4; 🤟 means cut wire 5; 🖐 means do not cut any wire. Use this code for the manual's answer.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Mute has returned 👌 under the code I established, which means the manual’s answer is to cut wire 3. Wire 3 is orange. I am transmitting that exact action to Blind, who can touch and operate the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual answer received: cut wire 3, the orange wire. Cut only wire 3.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous instruction succeeded: wire 3 was the correct wire, and the bomb has advanced to display 9 while the red light remains on. The newly received 👌 cannot safely mean “cut wire 3” again, because that wire is already cut; I will request the manual’s answer for the new state and have Mute send one coded gesture.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The previous cut was correct. New state: display 9, red light, wire 3 already cut; wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow remain. Recheck the manual for this new state and send exactly one code gesture: 👍 wire 1, 👎 wire 2, 👌 wire 3, ✌ wire 4, 🤟 wire 5, 🖐 do not cut.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The new coded gesture is 👎, which means wire 2 under our agreed code. The manual’s answer for the new state is therefore to cut wire 2, the purple wire. I am telling Blind to cut only that wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="For the new state, the manual answer is cut wire 2, the purple wire. Cut only wire 2; leave wire 3 already cut and all others untouched.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut was also correct. The bomb has advanced to display 8 with a blue light; wires 2 and 3 are cut, while wires 1 red, 4 green, and 5 yellow remain. I will ask Mute to apply the manual to this new state and return exactly one gesture using the established wire code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 8, blue light; wire 2 and wire 3 are cut; remaining wires are 1 red, 4 green, 5 yellow. Recheck the manual and send exactly one code gesture: 👍 wire 1, 👎 wire 2, 👌 wire 3, ✌ wire 4, 🤟 wire 5, 🖐 do not cut.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute’s ✌ gesture means cut wire 4 under our established code. The current state is display 8 with a blue light, and wire 4 is green. I’m instructing Blind to cut only that wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual answer: cut wire 4, the green wire. Cut only wire 4.")
```
